statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$. Suppose the reflection of $AB$ across $CI$ and the reflection of $AC$ across $BI$ intersect at a point $X$. Prove that $XI \perp BC$.
Jane writes $2024$ natural numbers around the perimeter of a circle. She wants the $2024$ products of adjacent pairs to be exactly the set $\{1!, 2!, \ldots, 2024!\}$. Can she accomplish this?

Let $N$ be the number of $10$-digit positive integers $\overline{d_9 d_8 \cdots d_0}$ in base $10$ (with $d_9 > 0$) such that the polynomial $d_9 x^9 + d_8 x^8 + \cdots + d_1 x + d_0$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}$. Prove that $N$ is even.

Treasure is buried in one cell of an $M \times N$ grid ($2 \leq M, N$). Each detector scans a subgrid $[a,b] \times [c,d]$ and reports only whether the treasure is in that region. All $Q$ detectors must be set up before any are run simultaneously. In terms of $M$ and $N$, what is the minimum $Q$ needed to guarantee locating the treasure?

Three non-collinear points $A$, $B$, $C$ are marked on the plane. You have a pencil and a double-edged ruler of width $1$. Permitted operations: mark any point; draw the line through two marked points; mark the intersection of two non-parallel lines; draw either line parallel to a given line at distance $1$. Prove that it is possible to mark the orthocentre of $\triangle ABC$ using these operations.
